::: {#sample-listings} ::: ## Past events ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false} ## Inequalities & Opportunities Summer School Hosted by the [University of Bari](https://www.uniba.it/en/courses/economics-finance-and-business), and co-organized with the [Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research](https://www.liser.lu/), [Sapienza University of Rome](https://www.dsge.uniroma1.it/en), the [London School of Economics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/international-inequalities), and [Queen Mary University of London](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sef/), this summer school featured 10 lectures across 3 thematic sessions: - **Intergenerational Mobility** - *Louis Sirugue (coordinator), [Francesco Bloise](https://sites.google.com/uniroma1.it/francesco-bloise), [Jan Stuhler](https://janstuhler.com/)* - **Social Welfare and Ethics** - *[Roberto Veneziani](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sef/staff/robertoveneziani.html) (coordinator), [Andrea Attar](https://sites.google.com/site/andreaattar), [Paolo Piacquadio](https://sites.google.com/site/paologpiacquadio/)* - **Inequality** - *[Giorgia Menta](https://sites.google.com/view/giorgiamenta/home-page) (coordinator), [Pedro Salas-Rojo](), [Xavier Ramos](https://bse.eu/people/ramos-xavier), [Domenico Moramarco](https://www.domenicomoramarco.com/)* The detailed program is available [here](summer_school_programme.pdf). ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false} ## Intergenerational Mobility & Migration Workshop Co-hosted by LSE's [International Inequalities Institute](https://www.lse.ac.uk/international-inequalities), [Centre for Economic Performance](https://cep.lse.ac.uk/), and [Programme on Cohesive Capitalism](https://sticerd.lse.ac.uk/cohesive-capitalism/), this event brought together researchers for 13 academic presentations across 4 thematic sessions: - Intergenerational Mobility and Elites - Integration and Assimilation - Intergenerational Mobility and the Labor Market - Migration: Impacts and Returns The detailed program is available [here](workshop.pdf). ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false} ## Smoothie seminars - Spring 2026 *“Accounting for intergenerational income persistence in a new cohort: Non-cognitive skills, ability and education”*
**Yuyan Jiang** (University of Cambridge)

*“Recessions, Educational Trajectories, and Intergenerational Mobility”*
**Matías Ciaschi** (CEDLAS-UNLP)

*“Earnings volatility in Latin America: evidence from administrative data”*
**Markus Nabernegg** (University of Giessen)
::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false} ## Smoothie seminars - Winter 2026 *“Grim Up North? Regional Intergenerational Mobility in Late-Victorian England”*
**Ziming Zhu** (London School of Economics)

*“Polarising Perceptions, Converging Preferences – How Inflation Narratives Shape Inequality Beliefs and Policy Support”*
**Victoria Hünewaldt** (University of Siena)

*“On decomposable median-based inequality measures for ordinal data”*
**Tom Gargani** (Aix-Marseille School of Economics)

*“Attitudes, beliefs, and support for economic policies”*
**Chloé de Meulenaer** (London School of Economics)

*“Monitoring poverty and welfare trends in data-challenging context: Recent evidence from various countries”*
**Hai-Anh Dang** (World Bank)

*“Using trusts in the UK: income, wealth and beneficiaries”*
**Sanaya Mahajan** (London School of Economics)
::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false} ## Smoothie seminars - Autumn 2025 *“Shifting Attitudes Towards Inequality Among Chilean Economic Elites Following the 2019 Social Uprising”*
**Rafael Carranza** (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile)

*“Family Background and Economic Mobility: Evidence from the US”*
**Alejandro Puerta Cuartas** (Universidad Carlos III)

*“The Role of Education in Explaining Economic Persistence Across Generations”*
**Valentina Gabrielli** (Paris School of Economics)

*“Structural Drivers of Health Inequality: Evidence from 10 Sub-Saharan Countries”*
**Mercedes Tejeria Martinez** (University of Cantabria)
:::
